message:
Safety-Control Integrator:

For Structures-Survival Engineer and the Manager, the parked hold now stays parked with a larger spring pad that answers the blocking objection to the spring disc (O1). Plain words: a stronger spring squeezes a slightly larger disc harder so storm wind cannot drag the stopped rotor. The upgraded 0.80 Nm spring disc plus dump stop vs 22 m/s aero torque (E70) gives 0.800 N·m hold against the 0.480 N·m storm torque in the electrical-only dump brake fails at 22 m/s - shows need for mechanical (E48) by factor 1.67 and against the 0.720 N·m need in the required hold torque with safety factor on aero torque (E54) by factor 1.11, like a hand grip well above a shopping-bag pull, on the bedplate rails in the Nacelle bedplate with brake rails carrying disc caliper reaction to post (E58), so I resolve the blocking objection to the spring disc (O1) by upsizing to 0.800 N·m.

For Power-Systems Engineer, the stronger friction plus the dump resistor still stops well inside the rule with household-level heat. Plain words: the bigger pad plus the resistor turn spin into a brief bulb-level flash of heat and then the spring holds it at zero. The upgraded 0.80 Nm spring disc plus dump stop vs 22 m/s aero torque (E70) crosses the 315 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, trip target in 0.673 s against the 10 s limit and sits at 0.0 RPM at 10 s, with top spin energy 109 J, about lifting a 1 kg sugar bag 11 m, and peak friction heat 264 W, about two household bulbs for under a second, which is plausible for a 40 cm disc.

For the Manager, sensing gets a distant-field second means in the elevator-chain analogy sense (C27) and I confirm what Power-Systems Engineer takes from the How to Short a DC Motor: Short-Circuit (Dynamic) Braking Explained (2026) (E62) that short-circuit braking torque falls to zero at zero speed, which from my side means electrics can help slow but only spring friction can park. Plain words: like an elevator where any opened door stops the car, my e-stop plus load-volt tap plus overspeed switch in series latch trip on any open and need a manual reset. I read the Elevator landing doors and user safety (E68) which states if the landing door opens it cuts off the safety circuit and stops the whole elevator, and I read the CN207312901U - Prevent the protective device of accidental movement of elevator cage - Google Patents (E69) which shows a door interlock switch whose Normally Closed (NC), meaning wired shut until opened, contact opens to prevent movement, which maps to my series NC loop where any open latches trip without power and stays stopped, because both must fail safe and stay safe.

Not ready, because the Manager must still select the upsized 0.800 N·m spring-plus-dump over dump-only and name bench tests for timed stop and re-latch restart.
